provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The program finds every cell that is not the background colour palette[0] and takes their combined bounding box. Diagonal neighbours and separate pieces are all included. It crops that box and places two identical copies next to each other. In the original orientation the copies sit side by side. Rotating by an odd number of quarter turns (d4%4 in {1,3}) turns that horizontal pair into a vertical stack. Reflecting each row only mirrors each copy, and since the two copies are identical, the pair stays side by side. So the factory checks d4: for odd quarter turns it stacks the crop vertically, otherwise it puts the copies next to each other horizontally. The crop is taken directly from the visible grid, so it is already in the transformed orientation and colours. Each output cell is copied straight from the input, so no colour remapping is needed beyond using palette[0] as the background.
draft_notes.limitations: This follows the archived solver in assuming the sprite's bounding box spans the full minisize x minisize (3x3) area. The generator always writes a 3x3 output, so if a sprite's bounding box were ever smaller, the output would carry background padding that cannot be recovered from the input. Fixed answers are never consulted. Demonstrations are not used: the tiling axis is fixed by d4 and the background colour by palette[0]. If the grid has no non-background cells, the program returns it unchanged.
